"Yes, this man bound the King of the Romans for us."
And by divine intimation, the word of mockery turned into reality.
Now, although the Sultan did not believe it,
yet he could not hold back,
but sent one of the youths whose name was Shādi,
who had previously gone with ambassadors to the King of the Romans,
to go and see him.
And when Shādi went and saw Diogenes,
he bowed down to the ground and prostrated himself to the king,
and ran to the Sultan and informed him that it was he.
And the Sultan hastened and commanded,
and they pitched for Diogenes a great royal pavilion,
and brought him there.
And they put irons on his hands and on his neck,
and a hundred Turks to guard him.
And in the morning he commanded and they brought him to him,
and he struck him four slaps with his own hands and said to him:
"Why did you not listen when I entreatied you concerning peace?" But Diogenes, because he was intelligent and wise,
spoke well-ordered words and said:
"Of all those things that are possible for a human being,
and which kings are obligated to do,
I neglected nothing;
but God accomplished His will.
And now do what you desire,
and leave off reproaches."
Then the Sultan said to him:
"Inform me now, what was in your intention to do with me,
if I had fallen into your hands?" And the king replied:
"Every evil.
For an enemy does not meet an enemy
except to do harm."
And the Sultan said:
"You have spoken the truth;
and if you had answered other than this,
I would not have believed you.
Tell me then,
what do you think I am going to do with you?" And the king answered:
"One of three things:
the first,
that you will kill me;
and the second,
that you will expose me to shame and parade me around your territories,
so that everyone may know and see your victory;
and the third,
I have no need to say,
because it is an illusory hope,
and far from being performed by you."
And the Sultan said:
"And what prevents you from saying it?" And the king answered:
"That you return me again with honor to my royal city,
and that I become to you like one of your patricians,
and when you call me, I will come,
and when you say, 'Do this,' I will do it."
